content.title: About
content.content: Carbonated flavored water is a non‑alcoholic beverage made by saturating pure water with carbon dioxide and adding natural or artificial flavorings. It contains no sugar, no calories, and is often used as an alternative to sweet soft drinks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial brand of flavored carbonated water appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
Flavorings can be natural (citrus, berries) or artificial, mimicking fruit tastes.
Dissolved carbon dioxide creates a mild tingling sensation that enhances flavor perception.
In some countries, flavored carbonated water is classified as “mineral water” if it contains certain minerals.

items.title: Sugar‑free hydration
items.content: Helps maintain body water balance without added calories or sugar, which is beneficial for weight management.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Moderate consumption may help relieve constipation by gently stimulating stomach motility.

items.title: Reduces sweet cravings
items.content: Flavored taste can diminish the desire for sugary drinks, supporting healthier eating habits.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Carbonated water has a lower pH, which with frequent use may contribute to tooth enamel erosion.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some flavored versions contain added sodium, which should be considered by people with hypertension.

items.title: Artificial flavorings
items.content: Certain individuals may experience allergic reactions or sensitivity to artificial flavor compounds.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drink chilled, use as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails, incorporate in cooking to add light fizz to batters, or mix with fruit juices for refreshing mocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the bottle tightly sealed. After opening, consume within 2–3 days to retain carbonation.
